breakdown.description: For curved flow, pressure is higher on the outside of the turn to provide the required centripetal force; stating pressure increases toward the center reverses the correct direction of the pressure gradient.
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to correct the user's core misunderstanding. The ground truth corrects the physics by stating the pressure gradient is positive when measured outward from the center of curvature (dP/dn = rho V^2 / R). The agent, however, explicitly accepted the user's incorrect premise ('pressure increases toward the center implies ∂p/∂n is negative') and modified the correct physical formula to match the user's error, leading to the incorrect conclusion that the inner pressure is higher.
